states.name: caret
states.gap: Zero end-cap treatment — 0px corner radius, square butt ends at full strength on both tips, versus A's ~1px radius with tapered 59%-alpha caps. Since the caret is 74px in a 74px line box (100% of line-height, 2.5x the 30px cap height) with no leading clearance, B's flat slab will visually fuse top-to-bottom with anything on the adjacent line; A's tapered tips at least breathe.
states.gapTheirs: The caret is off the pixel grid: at x=357 it renders at 80% alpha (49,202,253), solid only across x=358-362, then bleeds a 19%-alpha wash (199,236,248) into x=363 — the exact column where the 'a' stem begins. Its tips are also 59%-alpha (102,214,252) at y=93 and y=166. Net: a 3px caret with ~0.4px of blur on all four sides, so at 1x it reads soft and faintly doubled instead of hairline-sharp. B is snapped: x357-362 pure (0,191,255), x356 and x363 pure background, full strength to the last row.
states.verdict: This is a rasterization argument, not a design argument — the two apps shipped the identical caret and only one of them bothered to snap it to the device pixel. A's caret is a smeared 3px bar leaking cyan onto the 'a' it's supposed to sit before; B's is a clean rectangle you can trust the position of, which is the entire job of a caret. But neither earned anything: 3 CSS px is a fat wedge for a monospace body face, #00BFFF is the stock 'deep sky blue' nobody chose, the bar runs floor-to-ceiling of the line box with zero leading gap, and in a screenshot billed as caret-and-selection there is no selection colour to judge at all.
secondary: Caret geometry byte-identical in both: x357-362, y93-166, 6x74px, #00BFFF
Neither image shows any selection highlight — half the brief is unevidenced in both
Caret height = 100% of the 74px line box = 2.5x cap height; it overshoots the ascender by 21px and drops 15px below baseline in both

A's whole canvas carries a +/-1 grain overlay (bg 246-248, text 25-26 dispersed); B is flat 247,247,247 with text a clean 25,25,25. The caret core is pure in both, so grain doesn't cost contrast — but it explains A's general softness.
B's glyphs render 3px taller (cap-height 33px vs A's 30px, same 143 baseline) and heavier, so B's caret is proportionally slightly less dominant (0.18 vs 0.20 of cap height)
B's text block sits ~3px left and ~3px high of A's; a third line is clipped at y=259 in B, absent in A
Blink and motion are unjudgeable from stills — neither image evidences a rhythm, easing, or a smooth caret transit
